# PROGRESS.md as Build Log

An append-only narrative log of the build, kept in the repo, written per round of work. In
[[stickfps]] it is 40.5 KB across eleven rounds and it is **the real working record** — the git
history is a nine-commit import that says nothing about how the thing was made
([[import-finished-work-into-git]]).

Its structure has three parts worth copying: an append-only round-by-round narrative, a **rewritten**
state summary at the top (the only mutable section, kept short deliberately — see
[[architect-coder-tester-loop]]), and strikethrough on items as they are resolved, so a fixed problem
stays visible as history instead of vanishing.

## Dead ends are the payload

This is the one artefact in the entire source set that records what did **not** work. Nothing else
does — code shows the final state, specs show the intent, git shows a squashed import. From
[[stickfps]]:

- **No `reload-request` message existed on the wire at all.** Client-side reload was purely cosmetic,
  so every weapon was permanently empty server-side after its first magazine and every later shot was
  silently rejected while the HUD showed full ammo. Two systems each individually correct.
- **`WeaponRig` never rendered a mesh for two rounds** — a `return null` hiding a real [[three-js]]
  gotcha about camera-parented meshes.
- **Nothing tracked round wins**, so the match winner was undeterminable; elimination also advanced
  the round on the very next tick, making the death moment last ~16 ms.
- **Five authority loopholes in one round** — dead players firing, firing accepted in lobby and buy
  phase, no server-side equipped-weapon tracking, `joinRoom` leaving immortal zombie players holding
  60 Hz loops alive, and movement with no bounds at all. See [[server-authoritative-netcode]].
- **A real vulnerability**: the client-reported shot origin passed straight into the server raycast.
- **The ±π yaw seam** spinning remote players 360° ([[entity-interpolation]]); **lighting broke
  twice**; a **whole transport replaced** ([[websocket-tcp-over-geckos-udp]]); the **grayscale art
  identity retired** after being a mandatory constraint in three documents.

A code reviewer can find none of these from the tree. That is the argument for the file.

## Honesty markers

The log states its own limits where they occur ([[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]]), including
that one round was reconstructed after the fact:

> "Full input-replay reconciliation (re-simulating unacknowledged inputs after a server correction)
> is not implemented — v1 uses a simpler blend-toward-snapshot approach... Fine at low latency, will
> feel soft under real internet jitter."
> — browser_game_stickfps/PROGRESS.md, 2026-07-25

> "No commit made (user hasn't asked)."
> — browser_game_stickfps/PROGRESS.md, 2026-07-25

The second line, recorded twice, is why the git history and the work history diverge — and it is
itself logged rather than left to be inferred.

## Cost

The log is the only source for several load-bearing claims — the 108/52 test counts among them —
with no CI and no coverage artefact to corroborate, so those inherit `confidence: medium`. A
self-reported log is evidence of intent and sequence, not of a passing suite.
